newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand PM Chavalit declares war on drugs.
newsitem.headline: Thailand PM Chavalit declares war on drugs.

text.p: Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchayudh on Monday declared war on drug abuse in Thailand and said his government would make serious efforts to minimise the problem this year.

Likening the spread of drug abuse to the spread of the communist threat in Thailand in the early 1970s, the prime minister said Thai addicts spent more than 36 billion baht ($1.44 billion) a year buying drugs, particularly heroin and amphetamines.
"My government is declaring war against drug abuse and will try to make 1997 a year free of narcotics," Chavalit told a government seminar on how to fight widespread Thai drug abuse.

"A very conservative estimate found that local drug addicts have been spending more than 100 million baht ($4 million) to buy drugs for their consumption daily," he said. "Imagine how much the country wastes from this spending annually."
Thailand shares a common border with Burma and Laos along the Golden Triangle area, notorious for its drug production, and has been hard hit by drug abuse recently.
The use of amphetamines, heroin and other drugs has spread rapidly, narcotics suppression officials said.
The Office Of Narcotics Control Board estimated that at least four million people were addicted to amphetamines.
In the war against drug abuse, police have shot and killed at least 12 people suspected of drug trafficking over the past two months.
In the past 11 months, nearly 40,000 people were arrested on drug abuse charges and more than one million amphetamine tablets were seized from dealers.
The ONCB estimated that some 20 millions tablets amphetamines had been produced by drug traffickers in seven central Thai provinces in the same period.
